lessonTitle: Purine and Pyrimidine Synthesis, Salvage and Antimetabolite Drugs

blocks.text: A 6-year-old girl in remission from acute lymphoblastic leukaemia takes daily mercaptopurine and weekly methotrexate. These drugs kill leukaemia cells, but her routine blood tests also show that her white cell count dips whenever the doses are raised. The drugs do not know which dividing cell is malignant: both depend on a continuous supply of nucleotides for DNA synthesis, and the drugs sabotage the pathways that supply them.

blocks.markdown: **The idea.** Cells need purine nucleotides (adenine, guanine) and pyrimidine nucleotides (cytosine, thymine, uracil) for DNA, RNA, energy (ATP, GTP) and signalling. Two routes supply the purines: **de novo synthesis**, which builds the ring from small molecules at a high energy cost, and **salvage**, which re-uses preformed bases released from nucleic acid turnover at a much lower cost. Pyrimidines are likewise made de novo, with the ring built first and then attached to ribose.

blocks.title: De novo versus salvage
blocks.text: De novo synthesis assembles the purine ring on a ribose-5-phosphate scaffold, using amino acids, CO2 and one-carbon units, and ends with inosine monophosphate (IMP). Salvage converts free purine bases (hypoxanthine, guanine, adenine) back to nucleotides by transferring ribose phosphate from PRPP, catalysed by hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT) and adenine phosphoribosyltransferase (APRT).

blocks.markdown: **De novo purine synthesis.** Ribose-5-phosphate (from the pentose phosphate pathway) is activated by **PRPP synthetase** to **5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP)**. The committed step is **glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase**, which makes 5-phosphoribosylamine; it is inhibited by the end products **IMP, AMP and GMP**. The ring is built stepwise on the ribose from **glycine, glutamine, aspartate, CO2 and one-carbon units from N10-formyl-tetrahydrofolate**, ending as **IMP**. IMP is then converted to **AMP** (using GTP and aspartate) or **GMP** (via IMP dehydrogenase, using ATP). Each branch uses the other's triphosphate, which balances adenine and guanine nucleotide supply.

rows: Ribose-5-phosphate, glycine, glutamine, aspartate, CO2, formyl-tetrahydrofolate
Free bases (hypoxanthine, guanine, adenine) from turnover or diet
Brain, marrow, red cells (limited de novo capacity)
Feedback inhibition by IMP, AMP, GMP; PRPP is an activator
Product inhibition; depends on PRPP availability

blocks.title: Reading the purine ring's atom sources
blocks.prompt: Which precursor supplies the N1, C2, N3, C4, C5, C6, N7, C8 and N9 atoms of the purine ring?

steps.text: Glycine donates C4, C5 and N7 (the central three atoms).
Aspartate donates N1. Glutamine donates N3 and N9 (each amide nitrogen).
Formyl-tetrahydrofolate donates C2 and C8; CO2 donates C6.

blocks.answer: N1: aspartate; C2 and C8: formyl-tetrahydrofolate; N3 and N9: glutamine; C4, C5, N7: glycine; C6: CO2. The folate dependence explains why antifolates impair DNA synthesis.

blocks.markdown: **Salvage and Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.** HGPRT transfers ribose phosphate from PRPP to hypoxanthine (giving IMP) or guanine (giving GMP). In **Lesch-Nyhan syndrome**, an **X-linked recessive** deficiency of HGPRT, the bases are not salvaged: they are degraded to uric acid, and PRPP that would have been consumed accumulates. High PRPP drives glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase, so de novo synthesis rises, and the reduced IMP and GMP lessen feedback inhibition. Result: **marked overproduction of uric acid** (hyperuricaemia, gout, urate stones, orange crystals in the nappy) together with **neurological features**: developmental delay, dystonia and choreoathetosis, and compulsive **self-mutilation** (biting of lips and fingers). The brain relies heavily on salvage, which explains the neurological features.

**Pyrimidines and the thymidylate cycle.** Pyrimidine synthesis starts with **carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II** (cytosolic, using glutamine), builds orotate, and attaches it to PRPP to make UMP; UMP gives UTP and CTP. For DNA, ribonucleotide reductase reduces ribonucleoside diphosphates to deoxy forms, and **thymidylate synthase** converts dUMP to dTMP, using N5,N10-methylene-tetrahydrofolate as the methyl donor; in doing so the folate is oxidised to dihydrofolate (DHF). **Dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR)** regenerates tetrahydrofolate (THF) using NADPH, so the cycle can continue.

rows: THF depleted; thymidylate and purine synthesis fall; DNA synthesis halts (S phase)
PRPP amidotransferase (via nucleotide analogue), and false nucleotide
Block of de novo purine synthesis
Reduced GMP, so lymphocyte proliferation falls
blocks.caption: Antimetabolite and related drugs and their enzyme targets, given for pharmacology teaching; no dosing is implied.

blocks.title: Methotrexate clearance and the timing of rescue
blocks.prompt: After a high-dose methotrexate infusion the plasma concentration is 8 micromol per litre. Assuming first-order elimination with a half-life of 6 hours, what is the concentration after 18 hours?

steps.text: Each half-life halves the concentration: 8 to 4 to 2 to 1.

blocks.answer: 1 micromol per litre. Concentrations are monitored until they fall below a safe threshold, and folinic acid (a reduced folate that bypasses the DHFR block) is given to rescue normal cells; this is a pharmacology teaching example.

blocks.title: Why antimetabolites hit rapidly dividing cells
blocks.text: Antimetabolites interrupt nucleotide supply for DNA replication, so cells in S phase are most affected: leukaemia cells but also bone marrow, gut epithelium and hair follicles. This explains common toxicities such as low blood counts and mucositis.

points: De novo purine synthesis builds IMP from PRPP, amino acids, CO2 and formyl-THF with glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase as the regulated step; salvage re-uses bases using HGPRT and APRT.
Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is X-linked HGPRT deficiency, causing PRPP accumulation, uric acid overproduction, gout and neurological disease with self-mutilation.

Thymidylate synthase and dihydrofolate reductase form the thymidylate cycle; methotrexate inhibits DHFR, 5-fluorouracil inhibits thymidylate synthase and other antimetabolites target purine synthesis.

questions.stem: Which enzyme catalyses the committed, regulated step of de novo purine synthesis?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: it converts PRPP to 5-phosphoribosylamine and is inhibited by IMP, AMP and GMP.
distractorRationale.b: HGPRT is a salvage enzyme, not part of de novo synthesis.
distractorRationale.c: Xanthine oxidase belongs to purine degradation.
distractorRationale.d: Thymidylate synthase acts in pyrimidine (dTMP) synthesis.

questions.explanation: Glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase makes the first dedicated intermediate of the purine ring and is feedback-inhibited by the nucleotide end products, making it the control point of the pathway.

questions.stem: Which reaction is catalysed by HGPRT in the purine salvage pathway?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: HGPRT transfers ribose phosphate from PRPP to hypoxanthine (or guanine to give GMP).
distractorRationale.b: This reaction is catalysed by APRT, not HGPRT.
distractorRationale.c: This conversion occurs in the de novo branch to AMP.
distractorRationale.d: PRPP synthetase makes PRPP from ribose-5-phosphate.

questions.explanation: HGPRT recycles hypoxanthine and guanine to IMP and GMP, using PRPP as the ribose phosphate donor. APRT performs the equivalent step for adenine.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy has developmental delay, dystonia, and bites his lips and fingers. Serum urate is very high and orange crystals are seen in his nappy. Why does HGPRT deficiency cause hyperuricaemia?

options.text: Bases are not salvaged and PRPP accumulates, which increases de novo synthesis and degradation to uric acid
Uric acid excretion by the kidney is blocked
The brain makes excess uric acid directly

questions.correctOptionText: Bases are not salvaged and PRPP accumulates, which increases de novo synthesis and degradation to uric acid

distractorRationale.a: Correct: unused PRPP drives amidotransferase, and unsalvaged bases are degraded to urate.
distractorRationale.b: Xanthine oxidase is normal; it simply receives more substrate.
distractorRationale.c: The primary defect is overproduction, not reduced renal excretion.
distractorRationale.d: The brain has little de novo synthesis; its injury reflects its dependence on salvage.

questions.explanation: Without HGPRT, hypoxanthine and guanine cannot be re-used so they are oxidised to uric acid. PRPP also accumulates and stimulates de novo purine synthesis, adding to the load.

questions.stem: Methotrexate is used as an antimetabolite in cancer chemotherapy. Which enzyme does it inhibit, and what is the immediate effect?

options.text: Dihydrofolate reductase, depleting tetrahydrofolate needed for thymidylate and purine synthesis
Thymidylate synthase, blocking dUMP to dTMP directly
Xanthine oxidase, blocking uric acid formation

questions.correctOptionText: Dihydrofolate reductase, depleting tetrahydrofolate needed for thymidylate and purine synthesis

distractorRationale.a: Correct: methotrexate is a folate analogue that inhibits DHFR.
distractorRationale.b: Thymidylate synthase is the target of 5-fluorouracil, not methotrexate.
distractorRationale.c: HGPRT is not a methotrexate target.
distractorRationale.d: Xanthine oxidase is inhibited by allopurinol.

questions.explanation: Methotrexate binds dihydrofolate reductase very tightly, so DHF cannot be reduced back to THF. Loss of THF limits both thymidylate synthesis and the one-carbon units for purine synthesis, halting DNA replication.

questions.stem: Folinic acid (leucovorin) is given after high-dose methotrexate to protect normal cells. Why does it work?

options.text: It is a reduced folate that bypasses the blocked DHFR step and restores tetrahydrofolate-dependent reactions
It supplies thymidine to cancer cells only

questions.correctOptionText: It is a reduced folate that bypasses the blocked DHFR step and restores tetrahydrofolate-dependent reactions

distractorRationale.a: Correct: leucovorin is already reduced, so it does not need DHFR to supply the one-carbon folate pool.
distractorRationale.b: It does not reactivate the enzyme; it bypasses it.
distractorRationale.c: It does not chemically inactivate methotrexate.
distractorRationale.d: It benefits cells generally, which is why timing matters, rather than only cancer cells.

questions.explanation: Methotrexate blocks DHFR, so cells cannot regenerate THF from DHF. Folinic acid is a reduced folate that enters the pool downstream of the block, restoring thymidylate and purine synthesis in rescued cells. This is a pharmacology teaching example.

questions.stem: True or false: purine salvage re-uses free bases such as hypoxanthine and guanine by attaching ribose phosphate from PRPP.
questions.explanation: HGPRT and APRT use PRPP as the ribose phosphate donor to convert the free bases to nucleotides. This is a low-energy route compared with de novo synthesis.

questions.stem: After a methotrexate infusion the plasma concentration is 12.8 micromol per litre. Assuming first-order elimination with a half-life of 6 hours, how many hours will it take for the concentration to fall to 0.1 micromol per litre?
questions.explanation: The ratio of initial to target concentration is 12.8 / 0.1 = 128, which equals 2 to the power 7, so 7 half-lives are needed. Time = 7 x 6 h = 42 h, which is the type of calculation used to plan monitoring and folinic acid rescue.

questions.stem: A woman is a heterozygous carrier of an X-linked recessive HGPRT mutation and her partner is unaffected. What is the probability, as a percentage, that any one of their children will be an affected boy? Assume boys and girls are equally likely.
questions.explanation: Half of the children are boys, and each boy has a 50% chance of inheriting the mutant X chromosome from his carrier mother. The probability of an affected boy is therefore 0.5 x 0.5 = 0.25, or 25 percent; daughters are carriers or unaffected.

questions.stem: Compare de novo and salvage pathways for purine nucleotides in terms of starting materials, key enzymes, energy cost and regulation.
markingGuide: De novo: ribose-5-phosphate converted to PRPP by PRPP synthetase; ring built from glycine, glutamine, aspartate, CO2 and formyl-THF to give IMP
Committed step glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase, inhibited by IMP, AMP and GMP
IMP converted to AMP and GMP
Salvage: free bases (hypoxanthine, guanine, adenine) converted to nucleotides using PRPP by HGPRT and APRT
De novo is energetically expensive; salvage is cheap
Tissues such as brain and marrow depend heavily on salvage
questions.explanation: De novo synthesis builds nucleotides from simple precursors and is tightly feedback-regulated, whereas salvage conserves energy by recycling preformed bases. Both use PRPP as the ribose phosphate source.

questions.stem: Explain how a deficiency of HGPRT produces Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, accounting for both the metabolic findings and the neurological features, and state the inheritance pattern.
markingGuide: X-linked recessive, so almost all patients are male
HGPRT cannot salvage hypoxanthine and guanine, which are degraded to uric acid
PRPP accumulates and stimulates glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase, increasing de novo purine synthesis
Reduced IMP and GMP lessen feedback inhibition, adding to overproduction
Hyperuricaemia, gout, urate stones and orange crystals in the nappy
The brain relies heavily on salvage, explaining developmental delay, dystonia and self-mutilation
questions.explanation: The block removes the cheap recycling route and leaves PRPP free to drive de novo synthesis, so uric acid production soars. The neurological syndrome is attributed to the brain's heavy reliance on salvage rather than to uric acid itself.
